subject: EU data guardrails & SCCs — technical Q&A
messages:
From: Emma Blake <emma.blake@acme-corp.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Jacob Stern <jacob.stern@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: EU processing / SCCs — architecture questions

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we proceed to procurement, our security team has a handful of technical questions we need answers to for our EU-only processing requirement and Schrems II / SCCs evaluation. Please see the attached questionnaire (Acme-security-questionnaire-3.15.pdf) — highlights below: 

- Can Redwood guarantee that Acme data (customer content and logs tied to customer tokens) will be processed and stored only within EU regions (specific AZs) for both real-time inference and asynchronous tasks?
- Are keys (KMS) used for any encryption of customer data ever exported outside of the EU? Do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM) for EU-only deployments?
- What is your retention policy for audit logs and for backups/snapshots that might contain customer content? How do you provide deletion evidence?
- Do you sign the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as data exporter/importer or provide a template for execution? Any known non-EU sub-processors and their roles?

We'd like concise, technical answers we can include in our legal packet. If you can share a short written response and any attachments (SCCs template, architecture notes) ideally by EOD CET today, that would be super helpful.

Best,
Emma Blake
Head of Security, Acme Corp

Attachment: Acme-security-questionnaire-3.15.pdf (pdf)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Blake <emma.blake@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jacob Stern <jacob.stern@acme-corp.com>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:08:00 +0100
Subject: Re: EU processing / SCCs — architecture questions

Emma — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. Quick summary answers up front, and I'll attach a short technical summary and an SCCs template for your legal team. Ill follow up inline with Laura and our Cloud Ops team for any nitty-gritty.

- EU-only processing: Yes — Redwood supports region-restricted deployments. For hosted customers we can pin processing to EU regions (Frankfurt, Ireland) and ensure inference traffic is routed only to those regions. For Dedicated and Private customers you get explicit tenancy/zone isolation.

- KMS / BYOK: We support customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private (BYOK with HSM-backed KMS). For hosted plans we use region-specific KMS; keys used by Redwood-managed hosted instances are provisioned and stored in the EU. We do not export customer encryption keys outside the EU for EU-only deployments unless explicitly requested and agreed.

- Retention & deletion evidence: Primary customer content is deleted per customer policy. Backups/snapshots that include customer content are retained no longer than 30 days by default for hosted, can be shortened on request for Dedicated/Private. Audit/trace logs are retained 365 days by default; we can provide redacted audit logs and a deletion manifest showing object IDs and timestamps as evidence.

- SCCs / sub-processors: We can execute SCCs with enterprise customers; Im attaching our standard SCCs-executed-template.pdf for review. Our current list of sub-processors is included in the template; in short, core infra sub-processors have EU-region options and we have no planned cross-border sub-processing for the services that handle EU-only customers.

Next steps: Ive attached a short RW-EU-process-summary.pdf with region and KMS options. Laura (CC) will confirm a few operational details (log retention window, backup deletion SLAs). If that all looks good, shall we schedule a 30-minute technical call this afternoon (CET) to finalize?

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +44 7700 900000

Attachments: RW-EU-process-summary.pdf, SCCs-executed-template.pdf

Subject: Re: EU processing / SCCs — architecture questions (answers + attachments)

Hi Emma / Jacob — Laura here from Cloud Ops. Apologies for the short turnaround, below are the operational confirmations you asked for plus attachments.

1) Keys & export: For EU-only deployments we provision KMS instances in the selected EU region (DE/IE). Keys for customer-managed BYOK are HSM-backed and never leave the designated EU KMS. For Redwood-managed keys on hosted tenants we also keep keys in-region and do not export them.

2) Backups & snapshots: Hosted backups are retained 30 days by default. We can commit to a 7-day maximum retention for Acme on hosted if required; for Dedicated/Private customers you can select a custom backup retention policy. Deletion evidence: we produce a signed deletion manifest (object IDs, timestamps, operator id) and can include a hash digest of removed snapshots. Evidence is provided as a PDF export and we will store an audit copy for 90 days for compliance verification.

3) Audit logs: Default retention is 365 days. We can produce redacted audit log exports (timestamps, event types, operation ids). If Acme requires longer retention for audit, we can configure this in Dedicated/Private environments.

4) Sub-processors: Current sub-processors that may access infrastructure-level telemetry are listed in the SCCs template. To be explicit: compute/GPU infra is via an EU region partner (no cross-border processing for customer content). Monitoring and alerting pipeline has EU-hosted endpoints; support tooling may reach out-of-EU systems but does not receive or store customer content.

Attachments: sccs-answers-redwood-20270315.pdf (answers + manifests examples), RW-EU-process-summary.pdf (technical appendix)

Next steps: Mateo — please offer Emma two 30-minute slots at 15:30 or 16:30 CET if that works; we can run through the SCCs template and sign-off items on the mutual action plan.

Regards,
